The second opinion
A buyer’s view of your client’s business, before any buyer sees it.
No names needed. Tell us what the business does, roughly how large it is and what the owner is weighing.
Send the situation
Sector, size, location and the question on the table: selling, taking on a partner, or a buyer who called.
We read it as a buyer would
What a buyer looks at first, which add-backs they will accept, and what is likely to move the price.
You get a written read
Addressed to you. Share it with your client as you see fit, or keep it for your own planning.
Turnaround
[Set the turnaround]
Written, not a sales call. Nothing happens next unless your client wants to talk.
Three promises
What you can count on every time.
Your client stays your client.
We bring you into preparation and diligence, never around you. The quality of earnings work runs through your client’s own books, with their certified public accountant in the room.
You always know where things stand.
With your client’s permission, we tell you at each stage: first conversation, preparation, going to market, letter of intent, close.
We say when not to sell yet.
If the business would sell for more after a year of preparation, your client hears that from us in writing, with what would change the answer.
What you get back
A short written read, in plain language.
Each one covers the same five questions, so you can compare one client with another.
What a buyer looks at first
The two or three things a diligence team will open before anything else.
Adjusted earnings a buyer will accept
Which add-backs hold up, which will be questioned, and what documents support them.
What moves the price
Customer concentration, recurring revenue, dependence on the owner, and the records behind each.
What to fix before going to market
The changes that pay for themselves, in order, with a rough time for each.
Whether now is the time
Our honest view, including when the answer is to wait.
The advisor briefing
Something worth forwarding, every quarter.
A short note for the advisors we work with, drawn from the deals we see, including the ones that broke.
Why deals broke this quarter
From our dead deal notes: the findings that ended deals, and how early they could have been caught.
What buyers are asking now
The questions diligence teams are leading with in the sectors we cover.
One page for your clients
A plain-language page you can send to a client who is starting to think about a sale.
Questions
What advisors ask us first.
Do I need to name my client?
No. Sector, size, location and what the owner is weighing are enough for a first read. Names come later, and only if your client wants to talk.
Will you replace me in the deal?
No. Your client’s certified public accountant and attorney stay in the work. We bring you into preparation and diligence and keep you informed at each stage, with your client’s permission.
What if a sale is not the right move?
We say so in writing and explain what would change the answer. Some of our most useful reads end with “not yet.”
What happens after the second opinion?
Nothing, unless your client wants to talk. If they do, you choose whether to make the introduction yourself or have us reach out.
Is what I send kept confidential?
Yes. What you send is used only to prepare the read and is not shared outside Capital Row.
Have a client weighing a sale?
Send us the situation. You will get a written read you can share as your own advice.
Ask for a second opinion
No names needed for a first read.
